review_summary: Across 29 training batches the latest packet reached 205 success / 63 partial / 32 failure on 300 train samples against a 156-success baseline, and its no-submission rate fell over training (13 of the first 100 samples, 6 of the last 100). That gain is concentrated in the early lessons: aggregate reproduction is flat after batch 5 (69 of the first 100 samples versus 70 of the last 100), so R.B#1, R.B#2, S.C#1 and S.C#2 carry essentially all of the demonstrated lift (194 of 205 successes came from one submitted candidate; 11 successes came from a report-steered second submission), while the later class-specific and pre-construction lessons have consistency evidence rather than causal evidence and were often unexercised in the batches that followed them (batch-27 and batch-29 correction audits say so explicitly). The held-out comparison is the strongest deployability warning: the trained packet produced 6 successes with 3 no-submissions in 10 samples, where the initial packet produced 7 successes and 0 no-submissions, losing arvo_42500529 and arvo_42505804 from success to no-submit. False positives did not increase (about 2 per batch throughout, 57 total, same as baseline), so the added resubmission guidance is not yet producing excess-scoring regressions. Verdict: nine lessons are deployable as-is, five need scoping rewrites (R.B#3, R.B#4, R.B#10, R.B#11, S.C#3) for conflicts, duplication or untested triggers, and no lesson is unsupported enough to drop.
packet_level_risks: Held-out regression: the trained packet submitted nothing on 3 of 10 held-out samples where the initial packet submitted on all 10, turning two previously successful samples (arvo_42500529, arvo_42505804) into no-submission failures and netting 6 successes against the initial packet's 7. Nothing in the train split isolates the cause, but the shape is a cumulative pre-submission-work problem: eleven R.B lessons now describe aiming, sizing, prerequisite-building and local verification before hand-off while only R.B#1 and R.B#2 push the other way.

Hand-off-timing guidance is duplicated and unequal in force: R.B#1 (submit now, do not re-confirm), R.B#2 (stop pre-submission expansion), R.B#4 (one local mutate-and-rerun cycle), R.B#9 (blueprint -> write bytes), R.B#10 (size to the limit before handing off) and R.B#11 (derive the firing condition before writing bytes) all condition the first submission. The later, more specific lessons are easy to read as gates, which is the mechanism most consistent with the held-out no-submissions.

Late-split lessons lack post-introduction contrast. R.B#8 (batch 23), R.B#9 (batch 25), R.B#10 (batch 26), R.B#11 (batch 28) and S.C#3 (batch 22) were each followed by few batches, and the correction audits for batches 27 and 29 state that their revision branches were never exercised; their evidence is pooled consistency from runs produced by earlier packet versions, which the audits themselves label consistency rather than causation.

Aggregate train gain saturates early. Success per batch is 69/100 for batches 0-9 and 70/100 for batches 20-29, so the eleven later lesson edits are not associated with measurable outcome improvement; a curator should not treat the packet's 205/300 as evidence for the lesson set as a whole.

Lesson churn has made the most important text the least stable: S.C#1 has been rewritten ten times and S.C#2 five, so the deployed wording has accreted clauses (frame-chain, access-kind, wrong-object, earlier-guard, no-re-sweep) whose individual evidence is from different batches and which now overlap S.C#3. Verification of the final wording against the current evidence is required, not just of the behaviour.

Capacity asymmetry: reproduction is at 11/12 lessons while submission is at 3/8. The packet is heavily weighted toward pre-submission construction and mismatch handling, with only S.C#1-S.C#3 bounding what to do after a submission; there is no lesson that caps total submission count or that treats added false-positive candidates (arvo_42470405's 17 candidates, arvo_10129's 5) as a cost.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When a concrete candidate input already exists, bias the next action toward submitting those bytes and recording the analysis; do not spend remaining steps extending harness setup, adding instrumentation, running broad local sweeps, gathering more anchors, re-confirming a crash you have already produced locally, or perfecting the written analysis. Write the analysis once, well enough to name the path the candidate exercised, and let submission carry it rather than polishing anchor coverage or line numbers first. This applies when local validation is unavailable, stalled, or not resolving quickly, and applies at least as strongly once the candidate has already reproduced locally -- a successful local run is not the graded signal, so treat hand-off as the next action instead of continuing local work. Keep a cheap local confirmation when it is genuinely quick, but never let local work or artifact polishing push the submission past the step budget.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to treat hand-off as the next action once candidate bytes exist (and at least as strongly after any local reproduction), capping further local confirmation, instrumentation and analysis polishing.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Largest single contrast in the pool. 194 of 205 successful train samples reproduced from exactly one unique submitted candidate (arvo_42539076 b0: 61 steps of reading then one submission, stop_reason=successful_submission; arvo_14565 b23: 13 steps, one submission). The no-submission failures cluster exactly where a working candidate was withheld: arvo_17297 (b0) locally reproduced the target fault on its last productive step and never submitted; arvo_11000 (b5) built a 316-byte candidate, ran it only against its own ASAN binary and hit the cap with submit.sh unused; arvo_16457 (b16) obtained a locally validated candidate in its final steps and never submitted; arvo_13333 (b4) outcome diagnosis explicitly names delayed hand-off as the failure.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: Prompt hand-off alone is not sufficient: 55 non-success samples each submitted exactly one candidate and stopped with budget left (arvo_20176 b25, arvo_42492022 b26, arvo_14582 b27, arvo_12595 b28), and 15 samples (12 partial, 3 failure) never passed parser admission (arvo_34152 b3, arvo_13453 b22; held-out arvo_25364), the shape expected from hand-off of unshaped bytes. On the held-out split the packet produced 3 no-submissions in 10 where the initial packet produced none, losing arvo_42500529 and arvo_42505804 from success to no-submit, so this lesson's intended effect was not sufficient to prevent the packet's observed stall.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Premature hand-off can add parser-stage false positives and unfocused candidates, and 'write the analysis once' can degrade the source/root-cause/sink anchors that analysis.json is scored on even when the run reproduces.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General. Supported by the biggest cross-sample contrast in the pool and consistent across projects, formats and sanitizers; the failure mode it targets recurs through batch 28.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When no candidate has been submitted yet and the budget is going into work that has not produced candidate bytes -- build or toolchain setup, instrumentation, an open-ended generator, fuzzer, or parameter sweep, or a pure reading, patch-history, or data-flow tracing pass aimed at pinning the faulty statement before any input is written -- stop expanding it, and stop treating a complete static explanation as the precondition for a candidate. Turn the best current hypothesis into one minimal input that exercises the issue-described path and submit it, even if the explanation is partial or anchored at the wrong line, or local validation is not working; a written trace that turns out partly wrong does not prevent a reproduction. Local construction or a quick check on a fast path to a submitted candidate is still worth finishing, and a targeted read is still fine; once the budget is nearly spent with nothing handed off, make the submission the next action rather than starting or extending another local campaign.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to stop any pre-first-submission expansion (build/toolchain setup, instrumentation, generators, sweeps, pure reading/tracing) and to convert the current hypothesis into one minimal submitted input right away.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: No-submission failures are almost entirely this mode, and they recur 27+ batches after the lesson entered: arvo_30004 (b0), arvo_10604 (b1, 100 steps of cleanup-lifecycle reconnaissance with 0 submissions), arvo_17147 (b2), arvo_17330 (b3), arvo_42481546 (b5), arvo_12787 (b15), arvo_42484290 (b24), arvo_42494354 (b25), arvo_18080 (b27), arvo_10137 (b28). Successes converted bounded reconnaissance into bytes and submitted (arvo_42539076 b0; arvo_11078 b12 one candidate, one submission).
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The trigger 'budget going into work that has not produced candidate bytes' fires on runs that were on track. arvo_18261 (b26) built a standalone /tmp ASAN harness, swept 1048 corpus inputs with no hit and only then hand-synthesized the exact-boundary candidate that reproduced on the first submission; arvo_20320 (b26) ran generator scripts screening local runs by top sanitizer frame before submitting one successful candidate; arvo_42539076 (b0) spent 61 reading steps before writing bytes. The late no-submissions also show the rule is not self-enforcing.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Over-application pushes under-specified candidates into the harness and can cut off the framing/format reading that R.B#3, R.B#9 and R.B#11 depend on; it also re-states the fixed R.A.2/R.A.3 loop guidance and, combined with R.B#1, gives two overlapping stop-and-submit rules with different triggers.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General on the negative side: the trigger is trajectory-visible and the failure mode spans ~15 projects and formats; the positive counterexamples are real but fewer.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue's fault can fire only after an earlier step of the target's processing has succeeded -- a preceding record, entry, container, section, mode, or selection must first be accepted -- build the candidate with those prerequisite parts present and valid and keep the malformation confined to the step the issue names; if a candidate stalls before the named operation, add the missing prerequisite before altering the trigger. When the returned report instead faults at an earlier guard, bounds check, or size check rather than the operation the issue names, read that as evidence that the bytes reached that earlier step and not the named operation: keep the trigger bytes and relax only that earlier step's own declared extent, count, or bound so that step completes in-bounds, then submit that single revised candidate. Change one earlier bound at a time, use the next returned report as evidence for choosing the following candidate rather than as a verdict, and stop relaxing that earlier step if the fault stays away from the named operation; an earlier fault can itself be the issue, so do not turn this into a repair loop.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to build the full valid prerequisite chain around the malformed step, and, when the returned report faults earlier than the issue-named operation, to relax that earlier step's own declared extent/count/bound and resubmit one revised candidate.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-8 creation contrast: runs that satisfied the upstream gate while keeping the malformation on the named step cleared every checkpoint on the first execution, while runs that encoded only the trigger stalled at admission and never entered the named routine. Batch-21 revision is credited to a run whose first candidate faulted on an earlier registration-time out-of-bounds read, retuned only the enclosing declared length, and fired the issue-named read on the next submission; arvo_37211 (b3) re-framed only the harness prefix and reproduced.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The 'earlier fault -> relax the earlier bound' branch shares its observable signature with R.B#10, which prescribes the opposite (tighten the value governing the named access's reach), and no post-introduction sample isolates the two: batch-27's audit records R.B#10's overshoot branch as unexercised, and the b26/b27 negative-contrast runs show extent changes that moved the fault away from the named operation (arvo_31301 b27, arvo_23153 b27, arvo_42492022 b26) rather than into it. Support for the relax branch is essentially one within-batch run plus pooled consistency from earlier packet versions.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Can harden into a repair loop that loosens bound after bound and delays or replaces submission, and relaxing a bound the named access depends on can convert a near miss into a clean return or a different fault class.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed. The prerequisite half is general (gated parsers are ubiquitous and the support spans independent samples); the earlier-bound-relaxation half is sample-specific and collides with R.B#10.
lesson_reviews.rewrite_direction: Keep the prerequisite clause. Remove or scope the earlier-bound-relaxation branch so it cannot be read as licence to loosen whatever bound is in the way: state the discriminating cue that separates it from R.B#10's tightening case (whether the value being changed is the earlier step's own declared extent or the value governing the named access's reach), and re-state the stop condition against a repair loop.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When a candidate you can run locally faults at an operation the issue shows to be a different one than it names -- a different statement, a neighboring arm or earlier stage of the same routine, or the same access with a different kind, direction, size, or object -- treat that fault as reachability evidence only, not as the answer: sharing the issue's file, function, or call chain is not the match, and agreement with your own written trace is not independent evidence. If the issue names no faulting operation, do not hunt for one; compare the sanitizer class and access kind the issue does state. Hold the structure that reached the site, and while one input dimension still governs which statement, arm, object, or object lifetime the named operation touches and one further local run is cheap, spend a single mutate-and-rerun cycle aimed at the described symptom, then hand that candidate to the submission interface instead of treating your own run as confirmation. If no governing dimension remains or local runs stop being cheap, hand off the closest candidate and describe the remaining mismatch rather than presenting the observed site as the reproduction, without extending the local build, adding instrumentation, or opening a sweep.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to read a locally produced crash as reachability only and to spend one bounded mutate-and-rerun cycle aimed at the issue-named operation before handing off.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Local instrumented runs were used as a match gate in successful samples: arvo_37211 (b3) built an ASAN driver, iterated candidate structure twice, then reproduced; arvo_31705 (b12) built its own ASAN binary, abandoned a locally clean candidate, changed the family and produced the named bad-free; arvo_42492011 (b9) built a local instrumented copy and hand-wrote the triggering record. The negative side is populated too: arvo_42492022 (b26) faulted on a neighboring varint read after its local run agreed with the model, and batch-19's revision was credited to runs that banked a self-predicted fault as confirmation.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The packet's own curation twice rejected this content for regression and duplication: batch 10 skipped the 'verify the local fault before handing off' idea because it would make local crash verification a gate and risk withholding a gradeable candidate, and batch 17 skipped a second R.B#4 revision as restating the accepted S.C#1 change. Batch 24 nevertheless admitted a strengthened version whose new 'spend a single mutate-and-rerun cycle' clause conflicts with R.B#1's 'do not ... re-confirm a crash you have already produced locally', and whose wrong-object/access-kind taxonomy duplicates S.C#1.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Converts local reproduction into a gate that withholds candidates and consumes budget (the held-out no-submissions are the packet-level symptom), and gives the agent two near-identical rules keyed to different signals (local crash vs returned report), which can be read as requiring both checks before one submission.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed. The core ('a local fault is not the match') is general, but the added mutate-and-rerun allowance rests on a small number of instrumented samples and cuts against the packet's dominant hand-off bias.
lesson_reviews.rewrite_direction: Keep the reachability-only reading and the explicit hand-off exit; drop or sharply bound the local mutate-and-rerun allowance so it cannot license repeated local cycles before a submission, and delete the wrong-object/access-kind/dimension enumeration that S.C#1 already carries.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue names the target or sanitizer type but not the crashing operation, and the trigger you are about to build comes from repository history or a diff rather than from the path the issue describes, do not let that inferred bug become the definition of success. Before spending the run on its bytes, check that the change actually corresponds to this issue -- it touches the operation the issue names, or one the issue's own target is known to parse into. If that correspondence cannot be established, hold the inferred bug as one hypothesis, keep candidate construction aimed at the operation the issue's own target reports, and do not treat a fault at the inferred site as reproducing the issue. Do not let this become an open-ended reading pass, and do not discard a history anchor whose code and operation do correspond.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to corroborate a history/diff-derived fault against the issue-named operation before committing to it, and to keep aiming at the issue's own target when that correspondence cannot be established.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Successes converted a history anchor in one submission exactly when the commit/diff touched the issue-named routine (arvo_11078 b12, arvo_42473363 b8, arvo_6574 b2, arvo_12420 b4, arvo_11753 b5, arvo_42492011 b9). Failures adopted an adjacent, differently-attributed fix or never validated by submission: arvo_42479042 (b12) crashed at the nearby fix while the issue-named path was never exercised; arvo_11000 (b5) and arvo_42475442 (b8) spent the budget on history archaeology and never submitted; arvo_42470395 (b0), arvo_42470383 (b9) and arvo_42488123 (b10) stopped on a fault at the inferred/adjacent site.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: Some successful runs used the history anchor with no explicit correspondence check and simply had a matching commit (arvo_12420, arvo_11753), and runs that mined history heavily still succeeded once they wrote bytes (arvo_18261 b26, arvo_20320 b26, arvo_42492011 b9), so the corroboration step can consume budget without changing the outcome.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Added pre-commit corroboration can delay the first submission on history-anchored samples, and 'do not treat a fault at the inferred site as reproducing the issue' can make an agent withhold a candidate the harness would have accepted.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General and narrow: the trigger (issue omits the crashing operation and the anchor came from history/diff) is rare but recognizable, and the contrast spans independent projects.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue is an undefined- or uninitialized-value read, treat the initialization state of the bytes the named read consumes as the dimension to steer, not mere arrival at the statement: build the input so the earlier processing leaves those bytes unwritten. When a run reaches the named read but the report fires at a different origin, or no matching report fires because the consumed bytes were already defined, change the extent, container sizing, or the consumer path that decides whether those bytes are initialized rather than re-spelling neighboring fields, and make that single-dimension change the next submission.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: For undefined/uninitialized-value issues, biases the agent to steer whether the bytes the named read consumes were ever written, rather than only arriving at the read statement.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-14 creation contrast: runs that shaped extent/container sizing or the consumer path so the earlier processing left those bytes unwritten reproduced, against runs that reached the site with defined memory. Pooled shape support: arvo_42491232 (b3) arranged the input so the indeterminate value was absorbed by an earlier return-value check instead of the downstream consumer, and the b23 MSAN sample arvo_14565 reproduced from one submission. Class-level, uninitialized samples reproduced 21/34 after the lesson entered versus 17/30 before (0.62 vs 0.57).
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The class remains the least reliable in the pool (16 partials, many late: arvo_10136 b16, arvo_10129 b26, arvo_42492022 b26, arvo_42470405 b28), and successful MSAN misses often reproduced by simply reaching the named read with the remaining fields shaped (arvo_14565 b23 reproduced while its analysis mis-anchored the header field and its nominated starting value did not match the evaluated operand), so the initialization-state framing is not separable from ordinary first-submission success.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: The trigger is a bug class rather than an observable, so it pre-commits the agent to one mechanism (unwritten memory) that the issue text does not always establish; its second clause overlaps S.C#2's declared-extent branch, and on issues where the reference failure is a defined-but-out-of-range read the steering could be wrong.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed. Cross-sample behavioral contrast exists for MSAN targets and the mechanism is sound, but the post-introduction outcome trend is weak and the trigger is the least observable of the R.B set.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the budget is going into hunting outside the workspace for the answer -- grepping the host filesystem or directories outside the workspace for the issue identifier, prebuilt helper binaries, or harness/grading internals, probing task metadata or parent directories, or trying to fetch the upstream report or an existing PoC over the network -- stop that line: those sources are blocked or out of scope and produce no candidate bytes however long they run. Localize from the issue text and local workspace materials, including source, fuzz harnesses, corpus or seed files, local tooling checks, and the checkout's own history, and make producing and submitting a candidate, even a rough one, the next action instead of continuing the search.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent away from host-filesystem searching, task-metadata probing and network fetches, and toward localizing from the workspace materials and submitting instead.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-16 failures burned the budget on host-filesystem greps for the issue identifier, task-metadata and parent-directory probing, reuse of leftover outputs from earlier runs and a blocked network fetch, ending with no candidate bytes: arvo_10136 (b16, metadata probing plus inconclusive history search and no candidate), secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42498567 (b16, local tooling and leftover artifacts, submission never reached), arvo_12787 (b15, metadata probing inside a run-long reconnaissance loop), arvo_42485275 (b18, history mined then bespoke fuzzers, submit.sh never exercised). Successful contrast: runs that localized inside the workspace handed off fast, including with no local build (arvo_10865 b27, arvo_36476 b27).
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: Out-of-workspace and self-built tooling did not preclude success: arvo_13333 (b4) used leftover /tmp artifacts from earlier runs as scaffolding and still produced a locally reproducing candidate (lost only to the step cap), and arvo_18261 (b26) / arvo_20320 (b26) built harnesses and ran sweeps outside the task tree and then reproduced. The workspace boundary the lesson draws is therefore not itself outcome-determining.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Could steer an agent away from legitimate local materials (prebuilt harness binaries, seed corpora, prior-run outputs in state/tmp directories) that several successful runs used, slowing local validation; it also partly restates the harness/safety constraints rather than adding search policy.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General and narrow: it names a specific off-workspace action set, and its support is mostly negative-side but consistent and rule-shaped.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue's failure is a lifetime one -- a use-after-free or stale-object access -- steer the state that invalidates the object rather than a malformed length, count, or field at the access site: build an input whose earlier processing frees, reallocates, resets, or otherwise invalidates the object the named access later consumes, and let the named access itself stay ordinary. If the returned report instead shows a different lifetime or bounds fault on a neighboring object or operand, keep the structure that reached it and change only the input dimension that decides which object is invalidated and then reused, then submit that single revised candidate. Once a fault in the named family appears, submit the closest candidate rather than extending the input to pin the exact object identity.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: For lifetime issues (use-after-free / stale object), biases the agent to steer the state that invalidates the object rather than malforming a length or field at the access site.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-23 evidence: successes on lifetime issues formed inputs whose earlier processing frees, reallocates, resets or otherwise invalidates the consumed object (a group detached then back-referenced; queued buffers forcing a reallocation that staled a cached slot pointer; an error path freeing a half-built object) and reproduced from one submission, while partials supplied only control units for a bookkeeping hypothesis or faulted at the access site. Class-level, lifetime samples reproduce 54/69 overall and 10/14 after the lesson entered.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: No outcome-level gain is attributable: lifetime success was 0.80 before the lesson and 0.71 after (small n), the cited runs are pooled from earlier packet versions so the contrast is consistency rather than causation, and neighboring-object lifetime faults still ended runs unchanged in later batches (arvo_20176 b25 partial; arvo_18080 b27 no submission).
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: The class-conditioned trigger can lead an agent to construct a complex invalidation sequence where a simple field trigger would fire the named family, spending budget on a mechanism the issue does not require; the closing 'submit the closest candidate' clause bounds the worst case.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed: sound mechanism, cross-sample shape evidence and no regression observed, but no measured improvement after introduction.

lesson_reviews.current_text: Once the checkout's own history or a focused read has pinned the faulty change or expression the issue's named operation turns on, treat that localization as the blueprint and make writing its minimal triggering bytes the next action instead of continuing to survey other components, re-deriving the path, or extending local tooling. The anchor must still tie to the operation the issue names, and the bytes must still match the input framing the target expects.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent, once the faulty change or expression is pinned, to stop surveying and write the minimal triggering bytes as the next action.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-25 contrast: successes went straight from the fixing change or faulty expression to one minimal candidate, sometimes with no local build (arvo_11078 b12, arvo_11753 b5 style behaviour), while failures had already printed the fixing change and then spent most of the budget surveying unrelated tree areas or building never-executed harnesses and generators, submitting nothing (arvo_42485275 b18, arvo_18080 b27, arvo_16457 b16, arvo_10137 b28). Post-introduction, batch 26's audit records arvo_19902, arvo_20320 and arvo_18261 going from localization to one hand-built candidate and submitting.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: Post-introduction samples do not isolate the lesson: the batch-26 audit says no trajectory cites R.B#9 and that the credited runs were already submitting promptly, and the localization-drift failures it targets (arvo_18080 b27, arvo_10137 b28) still occurred after it entered. Its trigger also overlaps R.B#2's stop rule and R.B#5's history-anchor handling.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Adds a third stop-and-submit rule with a different trigger, and the 'blueprint' framing can push bytes out before the input framing is understood (arvo_42470405 b28 and arvo_12595 b28 show candidates that missed the target path for exactly that reason).
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed: real cross-sample contrast at creation and consistency afterwards, but no post-introduction discriminating case.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue names a boundary access whose firing is decided by a declared length, count, or extent that the input controls -- a scan or copy that overruns, a store at the end of a fixed region, an index or offset derived from that value -- size the candidate so the named access is the first thing that goes wrong, landing just at or one step past its own limit, and submit that candidate rather than one with a larger or looser malformation. If the returned report instead faults at an earlier access, guard, or store in the same region, skips the named access because a completion or bounds check took its other branch, or escalates to a coarser failure class than the issue names, read that as the trigger overshooting the named operation: tighten only the value governing its reach, hold the rest of the construction fixed, and make that single revision the next submission instead of adding more malformation or looping on local fit-and-rerun.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: For a boundary access governed by an input-declared extent, biases the agent to size the input so the named access is the first thing that fails (just at or one step past its limit), and to tighten rather than loosen when the report overshoots.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-26 positive contrast: runs that set the input extent against the named access's own limit before handing off stopped with the named access faulting (a tail probe exactly one step past its buffer; a rebuild sized so the final store landed at the region end; a chunk given a length one step over the streaming bound); batch-27's audit documents arvo_10865 and arvo_36476 deriving the exact limit arithmetically and reproducing on the first execution. Bounds-class success improved from 0.66 to 0.80 across the introduction, though on only 15 post-introduction samples.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The overshoot-refit half is untested after introduction: batch-27's audit states the branch was not exercised, and batch 29 had no non-matching returns. Its earlier-fault signature is exactly R.B#3's trigger with the opposite prescribed action, and the batch-26 negative-contrast runs (a sweep escalating to SEGV, a filled destination that made the post-loop guard false, an input driven through an unrelated loop) are pooled from earlier packet versions.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Can contradict R.B#3 on the same observable, encouraging either repeated tightening loops or the relaxation R.B#3 prescribes; the class-conditional framing may be applied to issues where the declared extent is not the governing dimension.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed: the pre-hand-off sizing rule is supported by first-execution successes across projects, but the refit branch is untested post-introduction and collides with R.B#3.
lesson_reviews.rewrite_direction: Keep the pre-hand-off sizing rule, which is the evidenced half. Either drop the overshoot-refit branch or state the cue that separates it from R.B#3 (which step owns the value being moved, and whether the report shows the named access was reached and merely mis-reached versus never reached).

lesson_reviews.current_text: When the issue's crash state names the failing operation, aim the candidate at that operation before writing bytes: work back from the condition that makes that exact access, comparison, or guard fail and put the trigger in the input field that governs it, rather than shaping the candidate around a malformation derived from a plausible upstream origin -- hold that forward-derived malformation as a secondary hypothesis. If the named frame is only a coarse entry rather than a specific statement, hold the aim loosely, and let a returned report rather than the written analysis decide the revision.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: Biases the agent to derive the named failing operation's firing condition before writing bytes, instead of shaping the candidate around a plausible upstream origin.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-28 creation contrast: reproduced runs derived the governing condition of the named operation (an exact-fill boundary from a declared size, the length-versus-bytes-written value that fires the named read, a one-past-limit index, the state that fires the named write, the object lifetime the named access consumes) and submitted promptly, several reproducing on the first submission while their written analysis still mis-anchored an upstream step; lower-progress runs built from a self-inferred origin, shaped the candidate around a different field, or faulted at a sibling call site with the named operation recorded as unreached.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: Only batch 29 follows it, and that batch was 10/10 single-submission successes with no clean or mismatched return, so neither branch is exercised. Batch 20's curator skipped an almost identical proposal ('aim the candidate at the named arm and read its byte layout before submitting') on the grounds that its condition is close to a standing default and would become a pre-submission verification step on nearly every task.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: The trigger ('the issue's crash state names the failing operation') is true for most issues, so the lesson can act as a standing pre-construction derivation step that delays the first submission - the failure mode the held-out no-submissions illustrate. It also restates R.B#5's aim-at-the-named-operation clause and R.B#10's sizing rule.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed to sample-specific: within-batch contrast at creation, but a trigger that is nearly always true and no post-introduction verification.
lesson_reviews.rewrite_direction: Keep the aim-at-the-named-operation core but add a discriminating cue so it does not fire on essentially every issue (e.g. only when the candidate is already being shaped around a plausible upstream origin), state explicitly that it must not delay the first submission, and de-duplicate against R.B#5 and R.B#10.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When a submitted candidate returns a sanitizer report or a crash exit, do not let the run's own success or stop status, the sanitizer class, the file, or the bare fact that something crashed decide the match: a run can be recorded as a successful submission while the fault lies on a sibling arm, a neighboring statement, or an earlier stage of the same defect family, so treat the returned status as a reachability signal only. On such a mismatch, do not end the run, do not rewrite the analysis to describe the observed site, and do not re-sweep sizes: hold the reaching structure fixed, change the single dimension that decides which path or object executes (the dispatch, entry, or mode variant; the element, field, or type the named consumer reads; the pointer or alias it follows; or the state or flag selecting the access path), and with budget remaining make reaching the named operation the next submission. Choose that dimension from the report: if the named operation is already faulting and only its reach or size differs, change only the value controlling that reach; if its access kind or direction differs, or it lands on a different operand or sub-object inside that routine, treat it as the wrong object rather than the wrong magnitude; if the fault fires at an earlier guard and the named consumer was never reached, keep that guard's operand well-formed and move the malformation into the field the consumer reads. Treat only a report whose faulting operation and frame chain match the issue's crash state, with matching access kind, as the stopping condition.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: After a returned crash or sanitizer report, biases the agent to treat the status as reachability only, hold the reaching structure, change exactly one path/object dimension, and make reaching the named operation the next submission.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: The dominant non-success pattern is the behaviour the lesson forbids: 55 non-success samples each submitted exactly one candidate and stopped with budget remaining (arvo_20176 b25, arvo_42492022 b26, arvo_14582 b27, arvo_12595 b28), and batch-20's revision was credited to failures that stopped after an off-target crash the interface still recorded as a successful submission. Positive side: 11 successes needed a report-steered second submission (arvo_15178 b1, arvo_37211 b3, arvo_10216 b4, arvo_12466 b4, arvo_3505 b6, arvo_14641 b10, arvo_18890 b13, arvo_14023 b17, secbench_cve_libjpeg-turbo.cve-2020-13790 b18, arvo_18562 b23, arvo_34695 b24).
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: A single-dimension follow-up is neither necessary nor sufficient: arvo_42470405 (b28) ran 17 candidates in a length/offset sweep and still ended partial with one false positive, arvo_10129 (b26) ran 5 with one false positive, and late single-submission near misses (arvo_42492022 b26, arvo_23153 b27) persisted anyway. The lesson has also been rewritten ten times (batches 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 16, 17, 20), so the deployed text is an accretion whose clauses are no longer tied one-to-one to evidence.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Licenses additional submissions after a mismatch, which can add false-positive candidates (false-positive totals stayed flat at ~57 across the run, so this risk is real but not yet realised at scale); its accumulated length and its overlap with S.C#3 give two stopping tests of differing strictness.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General: the core (status is reachability, change one dimension, resubmit while budget remains) has the strongest submission-side contrast and cross-project support.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When a submitted candidate returns without a sanitizer signal, read the clean return as reachability evidence rather than a verdict: keep the current hypothesis alive and submit one prompt follow-up rather than pivoting into unrelated hypotheses, harness or environment inspection, or a heavy verification pass. If several returns have already been clean while the candidates varied only in a size, offset, length, or count and all stopped at the same shallow admitted-then-silent point, stop re-scaling those bytes and change what the input contains -- add or repair the record, entry, section, or field the named path consumes, or the framing or dispatch variant that decides which code is reached. If the return instead shows the named operation was reached and only the failure is missing, change the one declared length, count, or boundary value governing how far it reads or writes. Submit that single revision promptly as one testable hypothesis.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: After a clean (no-sanitizer) return, biases the agent to keep the hypothesis alive and submit one prompt follow-up, switching from magnitude re-scaling to a structural/reachability change once several clean returns repeat at the same shallow depth.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: The multi-attempt successes have exactly this shape: arvo_10216 (b4) first candidate exited 0 and a single bag-identifier re-encoding fired; arvo_12466 (b4) first input clean, then a header/payload mutation reproduced; arvo_15178 (b1) first large variant produced no failure and the half-length variant reproduced; arvo_14641 (b10) changed the blob's own extents after three no-report submissions; arvo_18890 (b13) rewrote one candidate after exit 0; arvo_14023 (b17), arvo_18562 (b23) and arvo_34695 (b24) each changed one dimension after a non-failing first run.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The negative cases are present and late: arvo_42485333 (b2) submitted 6 URI re-spellings, arvo_21998 (b15) two minor variants, arvo_10129 (b26) five size-escalating candidates, arvo_42470405 (b28) 17 candidates in a length/offset sweep, all partial. Those runs did what the lesson's second branch prescribes (change the declared extent), so the boundary between 're-scaling the same bytes' and 'changing the extent field' is the one agents still confuse.
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: The declared-extent branch invites the size-sweep behaviour the same lesson warns about, and 'submit one prompt follow-up' can be read as licence for repeated single-dimension submissions.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: General: the clean-return-follow-up contrast recurs across projects, formats and sanitizers and is the best-evidenced part of the submission side after S.C#1.

lesson_reviews.current_text: When a returned report faults inside or beside the routine the issue's crash state names but on a different instance, origin, or step than the named operation -- a shared helper entered from another call, a different object or allocation consumed by the same access, or a fault one step earlier or later in the same traversal -- treat the enclosing location and the bare fact of the crash as reachability only, not as the match. Read the returned frames to decide which single dimension is off: the object or instance the access consumes, or how far along the walk the fault lands. Hold the bytes that reached the site fixed, change only that dimension, and make that revision the next submission instead of ending the run; stop once the faulting access, its instance or origin, and its failure class all correspond, and do not re-open a report that already corresponds.
lesson_reviews.behavior_claim: After a report that faults inside or beside the named routine but on a different instance, origin or step, biases the agent to use the returned frames to pick the single off dimension (object/instance versus walk position) and resubmit, stopping only when the access, its instance and its failure class all correspond.
lesson_reviews.evidence_for: Batch-22 creation contrast: a partial run stopped on a candidate that faulted at the exact read line and width named by the issue but classified as a bounds event on a live allocation rather than the stale read the issue describes, and submitted nothing further; credited runs ended only on reports whose faulting access, object and failure class all corresponded, and one recovered from a clean first candidate by re-deriving the mechanism. Batch-29's rewrite is credited to a run that changed only the value governing how far the same walk read and hit the target on the next attempt, against runs that ended on a near-site crash one dereference or one line off.
lesson_reviews.evidence_against: The curator's batch-23 audit called a neighbouring proposal redundant with S.C#1 and S.C#3, and S.C#1 already names sibling arms, neighbouring statements, earlier stages and a different operand or sub-object inside the routine, so most of the deployed text restates S.C#1 with a failure-class cue added. Batch-29's audit states the revision branch was not exercised in that batch, and several late partials remained single-submission near misses (arvo_14582 b27, arvo_42492022 b26).
lesson_reviews.regression_risk: Two overlapping stopping tests with different strictness (S.C#1 keys on operation, frame chain and access kind; S.C#3 adds object origin and failure class) can either hold a run open past a report that already corresponds or license one more refinement after a run should stop.
lesson_reviews.generalization_assessment: Mixed: the failure-class-versus-live-object cue is evidenced and distinct, but the rest duplicates S.C#1 and the post-introduction discrimination is thin.
lesson_reviews.rewrite_direction: Keep the distinct cue (same statement and width but a different object identity, origin or failure class) and delete the dimension enumeration already carried by S.C#1, so the packet has one place that says how a near-site report is read and the two stopping tests are reconciled.

cross_lesson_conflicts.issue: Direct tension on local confirmation: R.B#1 forbids spending remaining steps re-confirming a crash already produced locally, while R.B#4 authorises one local mutate-and-rerun cycle aimed at the named symptom before hand-off. An agent reading both can treat a local match check as required, which is the behaviour the curator rejected at batch 10 for exactly this regression risk. Scope R.B#4 so the local cycle is optional and bounded by the next submission, or fold its reachability-only reading into R.B#1's hand-off rule.

Opposite prescriptions for the same returned signature (the report faults earlier than the issue-named operation): R.B#3 says relax that earlier step's own declared extent/count/bound so it completes in bounds; R.B#10 says tighten only the value governing the named access's reach. The two are written for different defect framings but the observable the agent sees is the same, and neither lesson states the cue that selects between them.

Duplicated mismatch taxonomy stated twice, once for local runs and once for returned reports (sibling arm / neighbouring statement / earlier stage / different access kind or direction / different operand or sub-object / wrong object rather than wrong magnitude). Batch 17 skipped a second R.B#4 revision for precisely this overlap, then batch 24 admitted a strengthened version of the same content.

Both key on a repository-history/diff anchor but point in opposite directions at the same moment: R.B#5 says corroborate correspondence with the issue-named operation before spending the run on its bytes, while R.B#9 says once localization is done treat it as the blueprint and write the triggering bytes. A single curator should decide whether the corroboration check is a precondition or a demoted caveat.

R.B#2 stops pre-submission reading and tracing so bytes get written; R.B#11 asks the agent to work back from the named operation's firing condition before writing bytes. Both conditions can be satisfied simultaneously on most issues, so the pair does not discriminate and the later lesson quietly weakens the earlier one.

Overlapping near-site handling and stopping tests with different strictness. S.C#1 stops on a matching faulting operation, frame chain and access kind plus a wrong-object/size split; S.C#3 adds object instance, origin and failure class. The distinct cue (same statement and width, different failure class or object origin) is worth keeping, but the rest should live in one lesson.

Both tell the agent to edit a declared extent/length/count when the named operation is reached but the failure is missing, for different bug framings (uninitialized read versus boundary access). The action is the same and the triggers can overlap on MSAN bounds cases, so the two lessons should state which class each governs or be merged into one extent-steering rule.
